findings-against-prior-runs.prior-claim: source-path-anchor-resolves-its-chunk: pass — 'probe/dome.md#Dusk Operations' returned hash 3107e895 rank 1, chunkIndex 0, totalChunks 1.
findings-against-prior-runs.what-is-actually-true: The step could not fail on chunk selection: the file had one chunk and the bank one entry, so anything returned was 'the exact chunk'. With two sections of one file, the wrong section ranks first even with every floor off, and by default nothing is returned since 1.43.0.
findings-against-prior-runs.evidence: This run's source-path-anchor-resolves-its-chunk and full-recall-ranking-order items.
findings-against-prior-runs.so-what: Anchor steps must write at least two sections of the same file and assert the named one comes back first.

findings-against-prior-runs.prior-claim: memory-search-hybrid-retrieval passes only on a zero-overlap semantic query.
findings-against-prior-runs.what-is-actually-true: That shape proves the vector leg but cannot see a floor that drops keyword-only hits; the 1.43.0 floor shipped and passed a checklist that could not have caught it.
findings-against-prior-runs.so-what: The hybrid step needs the mirror image: a bare identifier query that only BM25 can carry.

items.expected-result: ADR-0106 D5: `--attach` (root and post-verb) is an unrecognized argument, exit 9
items.command: ai-raccoon --data-root <scratch>/dr --attach settings model show ; ai-raccoon --data-root <scratch>/dr serve --attach --port 0 ; read src/AiRaccoon/AppRunner.cs:50-77 and tests/AiRaccoon.Tests/Unit/Setup/CliArgsTests.cs:666-677 at v1.44.0
items.evidence: Both: exit=15, 'Unrecognized command or argument '--attach'.' AppRunner: a known verb's parse error routes through RunCliCommand and 'keeps ExitCode.InvalidArgument (15)'; only a verb-less launch returns FailedToParseCliArgs (9). The test ServeAttach_IsAnUnrecognizedArgument_Exit9 asserts parse errors and absent Attach properties only; it never checks an exit code (its comment claims 'AppRunner maps parse errors to 9').
items.observed-result: The flag is rejected, but with exit 15, not the 9 that ADR-0106 D4/D5 promise. The test named Exit9 cannot fail on the exit code.
items.acceptance-reason: Owner to rule: correct the ADR (15 for a verb-bearing command) or change AppRunner; either way the test needs an argv-level exit-code assertion. Not yet tracked.

items.expected-result: The 1.43.0 absolute-relevance floor (SearchRelevance.AbsoluteRelevanceFloor 0.35 on the content cosine, #646) drops irrelevant rows but never an exact keyword match
items.command: memory_write 'Error code AIR-4471 means the bank write lock timed out…' ; memory_search {'AIR-4471'} ; {'what does error AIR-4471 mean'} ; {'why did the bank write lock time out'} ; read src/AiRaccoon.Core/Memory/SearchRelevance.cs at v1.44.0 ; git diff v1.44.0 origin/main -- SearchRelevance.cs MemoryTools.cs
items.evidence: 'AIR-4471' -> results [] truncation [{'floor':'absoluteRelevance','threshold':0.35,'dropped':4}]. The two prose queries -> the AIR-4471 entry, fts rank 1 + vector rank 1, cosine 0.644/0.647. SearchRelevance.Judge drops any row with cosine < 0.35 whenever minRelativeScore > 0, whatever its keyword rank. Unchanged on main (1.44.1).
items.observed-result: An identifier, error code or path query whose only real signal is lexical returns nothing by default: the floor removes the exact keyword hit because its embedding cosine is low.
items.acceptance-reason: Regression from 1.43.0 (#646). Not tracked; #367 (hybrid RRF ranks near-literal matches worse) is related but different. Needs an issue and an owner ruling (for example, exempt rows the fts leg ranks).
